title: Cash Sale
tables: OINV ORIN ORCT OCRD OCRG OACT OBPL OWHS INV1 RIN1 JDT1 (v1's footer lineage string says 'OINV · ORCT · OCTG'; OCTG is NOT read — see traps)
blurb: What JIVO sold over the counter for cash rather than on credit, what those counter accounts actually owe today, and — kept deliberately apart — how much physical cash customers handed over against ordinary credit sales.
grain: One summary row per (SECTION, ROW_KEY); that pair is unique and checked. There is NO detail array — site/data.json carries `detail: {}` for all three companies, so this section has zero document-level rows (171 summary rows total: oil 76, mart 31, bev 64). A summary row means a different thing per SECTION: 1_SCOPE = one cash-sale customer card; 2_MONTH = one DocDate month of the register (plus a separate '(opening)' row for the 2024-09-30 migration); 3_BRANCH = one GST branch (OINV.BPLId); 4_WAREHOUSE = one dominant stock warehouse bucket; 5_CUSTOMER = one cash-sale card that has real documents; 6_TENDER_MONTH = one month of physical cash tendered on customer receipts; 7_GL_CASH = one G/L account (three cash tills + the 1101014 A/R control); 9_TOTAL = four grand totals over FOUR DIFFERENT POPULATIONS.

check.method: Recompose the headline from four independent GROUP BYs that the SQL computes in separate UNION branches, one of which (4_WAREHOUSE) reaches the number through the document LINE tables INV1/RIN1 rather than the header. All four must agree with 9_TOTAL A within ₹0.05 (each row is ROUNDed to 2 dp independently, so exact equality is wrong to demand). The documented one-time fourth route, not reproducible from data.json, is Σ INV1.LineTotal per document vs DocTotal − VatSum — it agreed to 0.0003 (Oil) and 0.0027 (Bev) rupees.
check.recipe: A = row(9_TOTAL,A).TURNOVER_NET_INR; M = sum(r['TURNOVER_NET_INR'] for r in rows if r['SECTION']=='2_MONTH' and not r['ROW_KEY'].endswith('(opening)')); B = sum(... if r['SECTION']=='3_BRANCH'); W = sum(... if r['SECTION']=='4_WAREHOUSE'); C = sum(... if r['SECTION']=='5_CUSTOMER'); assert max(abs(A-x) for x in (M,B,W,C)) <= 0.05. Repeat identically on INV_CNT with exact equality. LIVE: oil A=1363916.22 M=B=W=C=1363916.22 (δ 0.00); bev A=4311886.24 M=4311886.23 B=4311886.24 W=4311886.23 C=4311886.23 (δ 0.01); mart all 0.

check.method: This KPI exists to make a known defect visible, so its check is that BOTH inputs pass their own independent checks (cash-sale-open-diagnostic against customer-ageing RAW_OPEN, cash-sale-ledger-balance against the 1101014 G/L). Additionally assert the arithmetic that must NOT hold, as a regression guard: OPEN_INR − UNAPPLIED_RCT_INR must NOT equal LEDGER_BAL_INR — if a future edit makes it tie, someone has started netting receipts off the balance and is double-counting.

LIVE: oil v=326,368.87, guard=−44,431.16 vs a real +10,185.83 (differs by ₹54,617 — guard correctly fails to tie); bev v=5,453,800, guard=−1,419,204 vs a real −1,086,454 (differs by ₹3,32,750); mart v=0, guard skipped (no invoices).

check.method: Master data versus posting history: the net must equal Σ OCRD.Balance over exactly the 1_SCOPE cards whose ROW_NOTE says 'ctrl 1101014'. The two come from different tables (OCRD master field vs JDT1 journal lines) and are computed in different UNION branches. A mismatch means either a card moved control account or someone posted to 1101014 from outside the cash-sale cards — the note's JDT1 ShortName sweep proves nobody currently does.
check.recipe: net = row(7_GL_CASH,'1101014').GL_DEBIT_INR - .GL_CREDIT_INR; cards14 = sum(r['LEDGER_BAL_INR'] for r in rows if r['SECTION']=='1_SCOPE' and 'ctrl 1101014' in r['ROW_NOTE']); assert abs(net - cards14) <= 0.05; also assert (headline_ledger_balance - net) == Σ balances of the off-1101014 scope cards. LIVE: oil 8,901.14 vs 8,901.14 EXACT, and 10,185.83 − 8,901.14 = 1,284.69 ≈ KAMALJEET's ₹1,284.70 EXACT to a paisa; bev −1,086,454 vs −1,086,454 EXACT; mart 0 vs 0 with 0 lines (render as 'account exists, never posted to', not '₹0 movement').

kpis.label: Cash into the tills (all time, G/L)
kpis.formula: Σ JDT1.Debit over the postable children of the non-postable parent account CASH IN HAND (1105001 CASH SALE, 1105002 CASH IN HAND, 1105003 CASH SALE MAYAPURI), RefDate <= as-of, all TransTypes

excludes.label: Nothing — all TransTypes
excludes.why: the LEFT JOIN keeps an account with no lines reporting at zero (T10); this is gross movement, not the receipt route only

check.method: It is the denominator of the tender coverage check, so the meaningful test is directional: till debits must be >= cash tendered (C + D), and the accounts must be the same three in every book (the parent-child resolution is by NAME, so a renamed parent would silently empty the set).
check.recipe: till = [r for r in rows if r['SECTION']=='7_GL_CASH' and r['ROW_NOTE']=='CASH TILL']; assert len(till) == 3; assert sum(r['GL_DEBIT_INR'] for r in till) >= C.CASH_TENDER_INR + D.CASH_TENDER_INR - 0.05. LIVE: oil 3 accounts, 14,881,804.38 >= 8,297,884.75; mart 3, 29,703,569.01 >= 14,241,306.63; bev 3, 51,391,222.01 >= 47,099,680.01. All three books resolve the same three account codes.

kpis.label: Cash out of the tills (all time, G/L)
kpis.formula: Σ JDT1.Credit over the same three till accounts

excludes.label: Nothing
excludes.why: gross movement

check.method: Paired with cash-till-gl-in; the pair's difference is checked against a different SQL file (bank-accounts) — see cash-till-gl-net.
check.recipe: assert every till row has GL_CREDIT_INR >= 0 and (GL_DEBIT_INR > 0 or GL_CREDIT_INR > 0 or TXN_CNT == 0). LIVE: oil 15,893,408.23; mart 29,703,567.01; bev 51,159,169.00. Bev 1105002 CASH IN HAND is 0/0 with TXN_CNT 0 — exists, never posted to.

kpis.label: Cash still sitting in the tills
kpis.formula: Σ GL_DEBIT_INR − Σ GL_CREDIT_INR over the three CASH TILL accounts = cash-till-gl-in − cash-till-gl-out

terms.label: Cash in
terms.note: KPI cash-till-gl-in

terms.label: Cash out
terms.note: KPI cash-till-gl-out

terms.label: Cash on hand per the books
terms.note: oil MINUS ₹10,11,603.85 · mart ₹2.00 · bev ₹2,32,053.01. A till cannot hold negative cash — Oil's 1105001 CASH SALE is ₹10.23 L in CREDIT.

excludes.label: Nothing
excludes.why: see caveats — this is movement to as-of, which happens to equal the account balance because the go-live opening is itself a JDT1 line

check.method: A different SQL FILE entirely: bank-accounts.sql reports the same three accounts from the OACT side as CATEGORY='CASH_IN_HAND' with BALANCE_L / CURRTOTAL_TODAY_L in LAKHS. Scale by 1e5 and compare per account and in total. This is account balance versus journal movement — two genuinely different reads of the same G/L, and it is what proves Oil's negative till is real rather than a query artefact.
check.recipe: mine = {r['ROW_KEY']: r['GL_DEBIT_INR'] - r['GL_CREDIT_INR'] for r in rows if r['SECTION']=='7_GL_CASH' and r['ROW_NOTE']=='CASH TILL'}; theirs = {x['GL_ACCT_CODE']: (x['BALANCE_L'] or 0) * 1e5 for x in slice('bank-accounts',co).summary if x['CATEGORY']=='CASH_IN_HAND'}; assert set(mine) == set(theirs); assert all(abs(mine[a] - theirs[a]) <= 500 for a in mine)  # bank-accounts rounds to 2 dp in LAKHS, so the tolerance is ₹500, not ₹0.05; also assert abs(sum(mine.values()) - (TOT_CASH_IN_HAND_L * 1e5)) <= 1500. LIVE oil: 1105001 mine −1,023,420 vs theirs −1,023,000 (₹420, inside the lakh-rounding band) · 1105003 mine +11,816.15 vs +12,000 · 1105002 0 vs 0 · total mine −1,011,603.85 vs TOT_CASH_IN_HAND_L −10.12 L = −1,012,000. bev: mine 232,053.01 vs TOT 2.32 L = 232,000. mart: mine 2.00 vs TOT 0. All three agree inside the rounding band.

columns.label: Cut
columns.meaning: Which of the eight cuts this row belongs to. Rows from different SECTIONs are DIFFERENT VIEWS OF THE SAME MONEY (or, for 6_/7_/9_C/9_D, of entirely different money). Slice on it; never sum across it.

columns.label: Sort key
columns.meaning: Presentation order inside a SECTION. For 9_TOTAL it is the population selector A/B/C/D and is the only reliable way to pick the right total row. For 2_MONTH it is 'YYYY-MM|REAL' or 'YYYY-MM|MIGRATED_OPENING'.

columns.label: Key
columns.meaning: The identity of the row inside its SECTION, unique per (SECTION, ROW_KEY). It is a CardCode in 1_SCOPE/5_CUSTOMER, a BPLId in 3_BRANCH, a WhsCode (or the synthetic '(multi-warehouse)' / '(no stock warehouse)') in 4_WAREHOUSE, 'YYYY-MM' possibly suffixed ' (opening)' in 2_MONTH, 'YYYY-MM' in 6_TENDER_MONTH, an AcctCode in 7_GL_CASH, and a population name in 9_TOTAL.

columns.label: Name
columns.meaning: The human name, always taken from MASTER data (OCRD.CardName, OBPL.BPLName, OWHS.WhsName, OACT.AcctName) never from the per-document snapshot — OINV.CardName and OINV.BPLName drift (CUSTA001015 was renamed twice; Bev branch 2 is stored as both 'FACTORY' and 'Factory').

columns.label: Note
columns.meaning: Load-bearing, not decoration. On 1_SCOPE it carries 'ctrl <account> | grp <group> | active <Y/N>' — the control-account substring is the only way to know which cards the 1101014 G/L check covers. On 7_GL_CASH it is the role, exactly 'CASH TILL' or 'AR CONTROL'. On 9_TOTAL B it names the contributing CardCodes. On 9_TOTAL A it states in words that OPEN_INR is not a receivable.

columns.label: Invoices
columns.meaning: OINV documents only. Since the D6 fix it means invoices in every facet — receipt counts and JDT1 line counts live in TXN_CNT. Zero on 6_TENDER_MONTH, 7_GL_CASH and 9_TOTAL C/D by construction, not because nothing happened.

columns.label: Invoiced, gross
columns.meaning: OINV.DocTotal, tax-inclusive, in rupees unscaled.

columns.label: Invoiced, net of GST
columns.meaning: OINV.DocTotal − OINV.VatSum. The JIVO sales base.

columns.label: Credit notes
columns.meaning: ORIN documents. Tiny everywhere (Oil 1, Bev 3, Mart 0) — a zero here is real, not missing data.

columns.label: Returns, gross
columns.meaning: ORIN.DocTotal.

columns.label: Returns, net of GST
columns.meaning: ORIN.DocTotal − ORIN.VatSum — the figure actually subtracted from turnover.

columns.label: Cash sales
columns.meaning: INV_NET_INR − CN_NET_INR. CAN BE NEGATIVE where a bucket holds only credit notes (Bev month 2025-01 = −₹2,337.77; Bev warehouse DL-FG = −₹2,250). Zero on the tender and G/L facets by construction.

columns.label: Open invoices
columns.meaning: Invoices SAP still marks DocStatus='O'. Not 'unpaid' — see OPEN_INR.

columns.label: SAP-open residue
columns.meaning: DocTotal − PaidToDate on DocStatus='O' invoices. THIS IS NOT A RECEIVABLE. Cash-sale invoices never close because settlement is a lump on-account receipt that is never internally applied (JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0 on 100% of the 1101014 lines). Oil shows ₹3.37 L 'open' against ₹10,186 actually owed; Bev shows ₹43.67 L against a CREDIT balance of ₹10.86 L.

columns.label: Receipts never applied
columns.meaning: Σ ORCT.OpenBal on the same cards — money already received and already inside OCRD.Balance. Never subtract it from LEDGER_BAL_INR; that double-counts. Populated on 1_SCOPE, 5_CUSTOMER and 9_TOTAL A only.

columns.label: Actually owed
columns.meaning: OCRD.Balance. Ground truth. Positive = DEBIT, the card owes JIVO; negative = CREDIT, JIVO holds their money. Populated on 1_SCOPE, 5_CUSTOMER and 9_TOTAL A only.

columns.label: Transactions
columns.meaning: OVERLOADED BY DESIGN: receipts on 6_TENDER_MONTH and 9_TOTAL C/D, JDT1 line count on 7_GL_CASH. Never total it across facets. On the tender facets it counts receipts with ANY positive ORCT.CashSum, float dust included — Oil 2025-09 has 26 such receipts totalling ₹0.00.

columns.label: Cash tendered
columns.meaning: ORCT.CashSum on customer receipts (DocType='C'). A DIFFERENT POPULATION from the register: physical cash collected against ordinary credit sales, mostly by route salesmen. On 5_CUSTOMER it is the cash that card has ever tendered — unrelated to that card's invoices, and it is NOT part of any turnover column.

columns.label: G/L debits
columns.meaning: Σ JDT1.Debit on this account, all TransTypes, RefDate <= as-of. Populated on 7_GL_CASH only. Movement, not the account's balance — although for the three till accounts the net happens to equal the balance, confirmed against bank-accounts.

columns.label: G/L credits
columns.meaning: Σ JDT1.Credit on this account, same basis.

charts.title: How the cash-sale figure is built
charts.why: Draws the definition instead of asserting it: invoices gross → less GST → less returns → turnover, with the excluded migrated openings shown as a detached, greyed step so the reader sees the ₹24.42 L that is deliberately not in the number. Oil: 14,44,160 − 80,072 GST − 171 returns = 13,63,916, alongside an excluded 24,41,924. A table shows the five figures; only the waterfall shows that the exclusion is bigger than the answer.

charts.title: ‘Open’ is not ‘owed’
charts.why: Three bars on one scale from 9_TOTAL A, deliberately NOT a waterfall — they do not net, and drawing them as an arithmetic chain would be the exact double-count the SQL forbids. Bev reads ₹43.67 L open, ₹57.87 L of receipts never applied, and a real balance of MINUS ₹10.86 L: three bars make the sign flip unmissable, where a table row lets the eye stop at the first number. This is the chart that kills v1's red ‘Still unpaid’ tile.

charts.title: Cash sales by month
charts.why: Plotted on a real date axis so absent months read as gaps, not as continuity. Bev has no cash-sale rows for 2025-12 or 2026-01..04, spikes to ₹8.54 L in 2026-05 and ₹32.53 L in 2026-06, then STOPS — no 2026-07, no 2026-08. Ranked bars or an index axis would hide both the hole and the stop, which are the two things worth asking about.

charts.title: Two different cash numbers, same axis
charts.why: The single most misread thing in this section. Overlaying 2_MONTH turnover and 6_TENDER_MONTH cash on one time axis shows they are not the same money and not even the same order of magnitude — Mart's register line is flat zero for 23 months while its tender line runs ₹4.5–13 L a month to ₹1.42 Cr. Anyone who sees this once stops adding A to C.

charts.title: Which counter account the money comes through
charts.why: Concentration, with the cumulative line. Bev: CASH SALE DL alone is 95.8% of ₹43.12 L. Oil: HARPREET 71.4%, KAMALJEET 28.5%. A three-row table shows the same numbers; the cumulative line shows that ‘cash sales’ in Beverages is effectively one account, which is what makes the next chart worth drawing.

charts.title: Counter sale or wholesale wearing a counter card?
charts.why: Plots invoice count against average ticket per card, bubble-sized by turnover. Oil's cards cluster where a counter belongs — 1,012 invoices at ₹1,014 each. Bev's CASH SALE DL sits alone at 98 invoices averaging ₹44,449. No table column says ‘this card is not behaving like a counter’; the position on this chart does. Flagged as an open question in the section note, not as a finding.

charts.title: Which godown the counter sells out of
charts.why: Ten Oil buckets and six Bev buckets, area-proportional, so the long tail is visible without a scroll — Oil's BH-FG (₹4.01 L) and DL-J3 (₹3.89 L) against seven buckets under ₹1 L. Negative and synthetic buckets cannot be tiled and are listed beside it instead: Bev DL-FG −₹2,250 (credit notes only) and the '(multi-warehouse)' bucket (Oil 14 docs ₹21,470, Bev 2 docs ₹2,883), which is a bucket rather than an apportionment.

charts.title: How much of the till movement the receipt route explains
charts.series: (9_TOTAL C + D) / Σ CASH TILL GL_DEBIT_INR
charts.why: Turns the cross-check into something a reader can see the strength of: Bev 91.6%, Oil 55.8%, Mart 47.9%. A green tick claiming ‘verified’ would be dishonest at 47.9% — the meter says how much of the G/L the ORCT route actually accounts for, and the uncovered part is named (till-to-till transfers, storno reversals, cancelled receipts, vendor refunds), so a low reading is informative rather than alarming.

traps: FACETED — summing every row multiplies the register by about six. The register total is the single row where SECTION == '9_TOTAL' AND SORT_KEY == 'A' (ROW_KEY 'CASH_SALE_INVOICES'). SORT_KEY, not position: never take rows[0] of the 9_TOTAL group.

There are FOUR 9_TOTAL rows and they are FOUR DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. A = cash-sale invoices, B = migrated go-live openings, C = physical cash tendered by external customers, D = the same cash from group/branch cards. A + C is invoices plus receipts and means nothing. Never donut, stack or total them together.

2_MONTH contains the migrated openings under ROW_KEY '2024-09 (opening)'. Summing 2_MONTH unfiltered gives Oil ₹38,86,084 gross against a ₹14,44,160 headline (2.7×). Filter on SORT_KEY not ending '|MIGRATED_OPENING' (or ROW_KEY not ending ' (opening)'). This exact bug was live in 3_BRANCH/4_WAREHOUSE/5_CUSTOMER until the D1 fix.

OPEN_INR is NOT a receivable (C-0019, trap T6). Cash-sale invoices stay DocStatus='O' forever — JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0 on 100% of the 1101014 lines. Oil: ₹3,36,555 'open' against ₹10,186 actually owed, 33×. Bev: ₹43,67,346 'open' against a CREDIT balance of ₹10,86,454 — the sign is wrong, not just the size. LEDGER_BAL_INR is the only figure that answers 'what do they owe'.

Never subtract UNAPPLIED_RCT_INR from LEDGER_BAL_INR — the receipt is already inside OCRD.Balance. They also do not tie: Oil OPEN − UNAPPLIED = −₹44,431 against a real +₹10,186; Bev −₹14,19,204 against a real −₹10,86,454. If a future build makes them tie, someone has started double-counting.

LIVE v1 BUG, do not carry forward: site/index.html renders a red KPI 'Still unpaid — a cash sale should not carry a balance' straight off OPEN_INR. On Beverages that publishes ₹43.67 L as unpaid for an account that is ₹10.86 L in credit. v1 shows neither UNAPPLIED_RCT_INR nor LEDGER_BAL_INR anywhere on the page.

LIVE v1 BUG: v1's '7_GL_CASH — Cross-check against the cash ledger' table is configured with cols ['ROW_LABEL','ROW_NOTE','INV_CNT','TURNOVER_NET_INR']. Those two measures are structurally 0 on every 7_GL_CASH row. The cross-check panel renders four rows of zeros. The populated columns are TXN_CNT, GL_DEBIT_INR and GL_CREDIT_INR.

LIVE v1 BUG: v1 renders no tender block at all — 6_TENDER_MONTH and 9_TOTAL C/D are absent from the page, so ₹4.71 Cr (Bev) and ₹1.42 Cr (Mart) of physical cash are invisible, and Mart's page reads 'Cash sales ₹0' as though Mart handles no cash. 9_TOTAL B (Oil's ₹24.42 L of openings) is also never shown.

TXN_CNT is overloaded: receipts on 6_TENDER_MONTH and 9_TOTAL C/D, JDT1 line count on 7_GL_CASH. Totalling the column across the section is meaningless (Oil would read 1,076 receipts + 2,847 journal lines as one number).

TXN_CNT on the tender facets counts receipts with ANY positive ORCT.CashSum, including sub-paise float residue. Oil 2025-09 = 26 receipts totalling ₹0.00, Oil 2026-08 = 7 receipts ₹0.00, Bev 9_TOTAL D = 2 receipts ₹0.00. A count of cash receipts is not a count of cash, and ₹0.00 beside a non-zero count must never render as 'no cash'.

GL_DEBIT_INR / GL_CREDIT_INR are all-time JDT1 movement to the as-of date across ALL TransTypes, not the receipt route and not, on its face, an account balance. Oil's three tills net to MINUS ₹10,11,604. That is confirmed independently by bank-accounts (TOT_CASH_IN_HAND_L = −10.12 L, 1105001 BALANCE_L = −10.23 L), so it is real, not a query artefact — but a till cannot physically hold negative cash. Present it as a flagged G/L position, never as 'cash in hand'.

The cash-sale scope is NOT a subset of the receivables TRADE population. Oil CUSTA000886 KAMALPREET SINGH (CASH SALE) is ACCT_KIND 'STAFF' with IS_EXCLUDED = 1 in customer-ageing, yet sits inside the cash-sale register. Cash-sale turnover therefore cannot be reconciled against the receivables TRADE headline.

Two cash-sale cards do not post to 1101014 (Oil CUSTA001015 → 1101008 CALL CENTRE, CUSTA000250 → 1101005 E-COM; Bev CUSTA000250 → 1101005). The 1101014 G/L check therefore covers only the on-1101014 subset. Oil's ₹1,284.69 gap between the G/L net and the headline balance is exactly KAMALJEET's balance — expected, not a break. Read the 'ctrl <account>' substring in 1_SCOPE.ROW_NOTE before asserting the check.

Do NOT cross-check this section against open-item-list. That query keeps only items with OPEN_AMT >= ₹10,000 and then caps at the top 1,500 by size or top 400 per doctype (open-item-list.sql lines 412 and 419). Oil returns ZERO open-item rows for the cash-sale cards even though the register holds 259 open documents; Bev ties exactly only because its items are large. Use customer-ageing detail, which is complete per card.

TURNOVER_NET_INR can be negative in a bucket that holds only credit notes: Bev month 2025-01 = −₹2,337.77 and Bev warehouse DL-FG = −₹2,250 (INV_CNT 0, one credit note). Treemaps and donuts cannot render it; clip it out of those and list it beside them, never clamp it to zero.

2_MONTH is not zero-filled — an absent month means no documents, not a zero month. Bev jumps 2025-11 → 2026-05 and ends at 2026-06 with nothing in July or August 2026. Plot on a real date axis or the trend line lies.

OCTG is in v1's lineage string ('OINV · ORCT · OCTG') but cash-sale.sql never reads it. Payment terms were tested as the cash-sale marker and DISPROVEN: term −1 'ADVANCE/CASH/0 DAYS' is SAP's default bucket, 15,586 Oil invoices worth ₹925.91 Cr; term 10 'COD' is 39 invoices. So are POS fields (all 0/blank on 31,027 Oil invoices), OINV.DocType (only 'I'/'S'), and DocDueDate = DocDate (14,820 Oil invoices, ₹879 Cr, topped by intercompany). Do not reintroduce any of them.

Name-matching '%CASH%' is wrong: it catches CASHEW, METRO CASH & CARRY (a ₹66.4 L credit customer), CASH PURCHASE HR and ONE97 CASH BACK. Scope = control account 1101014 OR the phrase 'CASH SALE', barring '%CASH & CARRY%', with CardType = 'C'.

C-0021: CANCELED on OINV/ORIN is three-valued N / Y / C (C is the reversing document). Oil OINV = 1,129 N, 18 Y, 18 C at ₹29,885 each side — filtering '<> Y' inflates Oil by ₹29,885. ORCT spells the column 'Canceled' and carries only Y/N.

Labels come from master data, keys from ids. OINV.CardName and OINV.BPLName are per-document snapshots: CUSTA001015 was BALWINDER KAUR J/3 → KAMAL J3 PAYMENTS → KAMALJEET CASH SALE J3, and Bev branch 2 is stored as both 'FACTORY' (97 docs) and 'Factory' (7), which used to emit two rows keyed '2'. Group on BPLId / CardCode, label from OBPL / OCRD.

4_WAREHOUSE is a bucket, not an apportionment. A document touching more than one warehouse lands whole in the synthetic '(multi-warehouse)' row (Oil 14 docs ₹21,470; Bev 2 docs ₹2,883); nothing is split by value, so the facet still totals correctly but no single warehouse figure is a true value split.

Rounding: every row is ROUNDed to 2 dp independently while the 9_TOTAL row rounds the unrounded sum, so facet recompositions land up to about ₹0.03 away. Oil's LEDGER_BAL_INR is 10,185.83 on 9_TOTAL A but 10,185.84 by summing 1_SCOPE. Equality checks need a ±₹0.05 tolerance; anything tighter will show a permanent red dot.

The migrated-opening test is DocDate = 2024-09-30 exactly. A genuine cash sale ever back-dated to the go-live date would be silently misfiled into 9_TOTAL B and dropped from the headline. There is no SAP flag that distinguishes them.

Oil's CASH SALE PB (CUSTA000893) has ₹56,750 of journal-entry movement on 1101014 and zero invoices. It appears in 1_SCOPE and in no other facet, so its money exists only inside 7_GL_CASH. The register is an INVOICE register; not all 1101014 money is in it (Oil: ₹35,92,328 of G/L debits vs ₹34,64,703 of invoices on the 1101014 cards, the ₹1,22,245 gap itemised as ₹56,750 CASH SALE PB + ₹58,995 HARPREET + ₹6,500 KAMALPREET journal entries).

This section emits NO detail rows (data.json carries detail = {} for all three companies). Nothing on this page can drill to a document. Any 'see the invoices' affordance must say so; the deepest available drill is the party ledger via 1_SCOPE / 5_CUSTOMER CardCode and the G/L account via 7_GL_CASH ROW_KEY.

FOUR KPIs are DERIVED — their `live` value is NOT agg(column) and a page that renders the named column raw will publish the wrong number: cash-sale-ar-control-gl-net = GL_DEBIT_INR − GL_CREDIT_INR (raw column gives Oil ₹35,92,328 instead of ₹8,901.14); cash-till-gl-net = Σ GL_DEBIT_INR − Σ GL_CREDIT_INR (raw gives Oil ₹1,48,81,804 instead of −₹10,11,604); cash-sale-open-overstatement = OPEN_INR − LEDGER_BAL_INR; cash-sale-avg-ticket = INV_GROSS_INR ÷ INV_CNT; and cash-sale-card-count is COUNT(rows), not a sum of ROW_KEY. Read `formula`, never `column` alone. Every other KPI is agg(column) over row_filter and verified as such.
empty_states: Mart's register is a VERIFIED ZERO, not a failure and not unknown: 9_TOTAL A is all zeros because Mart books no cash-sale documents at all, while three cash-sale cards exist (two flagged validFor = 'N') with nil balances and account 1101014 exists with zero JDT1 lines. Render '₹0' only with that sentence attached; the raw zero on its own is the exact 'confident zero' the contract bans. (Before the D4 fix this row came back all-NULL and v1 printed em dashes, reading as 'unknown'.)

Mart has no 2_MONTH, 3_BRANCH, 4_WAREHOUSE or 5_CUSTOMER rows at all (31 rows: 3 scope + 20 tender months + 4 G/L + 4 totals). Every register breakdown panel must render empty('Mart books no cash-sale invoices, so there is nothing to break down — but it did collect ₹1.42 Cr of physical cash, below') and link down to the tender block, never draw an axis with no bars.
9_TOTAL D with TXN_CNT > 0 and CASH_TENDER_INR == 0 (Beverages: 2 receipts, ₹0.00): render '2 receipts flagged as cash, total below ₹0.01', never '₹0' and never 'no group cash'.

6_TENDER_MONTH months with TXN_CNT > 0 and CASH_TENDER_INR == 0 (Oil 2025-09 n = 26, Oil 2026-08 n = 7): same treatment. On the month chart draw the point at zero but mark it, because a plain zero implies no receipts when there were 26.

7_GL_CASH rows with TXN_CNT == 0 (Mart 1101014, Bev 1105002 CASH IN HAND): render 'account exists, never posted to' rather than '₹0 movement' — the LEFT JOIN exists precisely so these rows appear instead of vanishing, and a bare zero throws that information away.

Any KPI whose 9_TOTAL row is missing from the slice (a partial build) renders not-computed with the missing SORT_KEY named. Never fall back to rows[0] of the 9_TOTAL group and never treat a missing row as zero.
cash-sale-avg-ticket is undefined when INV_CNT == 0 (Mart). Render 'no invoices to average', not '₹0'.
GST implied rate (INV_GROSS − INV_NET) / INV_NET is undefined for Mart; skip the check rather than reporting 0%.
cash-tender-group has no second route computable from data.json — C and D partition one CTE. Its check dot must render as 'single route' (grey), not green. Claiming verification there would be false.
The cash-tender coverage meter must show its own denominator: at Mart's 47.9% the check is weak, and the panel says which movements are outside the ORCT route rather than implying a failure.

If sections['cash-sale'].errors is non-empty for a company, or the company key is absent from summary, the whole page renders empty() with the pipeline error text and the generated_at stamp. Never a zero, never a dash.
Any document-level drill target renders empty('cash-sale emits no document-level rows — open the party ledger instead') with the party link, rather than an empty table with headers.
